one_line_contribution: An intervention-anchored (REPLACE-static, token-matched) measurement of how much a learned per-item memory utility is still worth after three ordinary changes - reader swap, store growth, layout shift - each with its own re-measurement-noise control, predicting that the value of planted harmful items survives these changes while the value of helpful expert items does not, plus a cost curve of re-probing versus re-learning the utility under the new reader.
closest_prior_work: arXiv:2605.30712 (verified by s2cli search on the S2 channel; note it is indexed as 'ExpGraph: Model-Agnostic Experience Learning with Graph-Structured Memory for LLM Agents', not 'ExpSuite' as the proposal calls it) is the sharpest threat and also the sharpest foil: it explicitly claims utility-aware ranking that supports 'experience reuse across diverse tasks and executor models'. It does not scoop the proposal, because its evidence is aggregate task success under different executors, with no re-measurement of any individual item's value under the swapped executor and no separation of helpful from harmful items - which is precisely the gap here. Two secondary threats are real. arXiv:2607.10608 (The Compliance Trap, verified) already establishes, at trajectory level, that conflicting memory harms agents and harms stronger agents more; the 'harm transfers' half of the headline is therefore substantially anticipated, and the proposal's own Related Work concedes this by using it as the source of the reverse outcome. arXiv:2608.04574 (When Memory Lies: An Empirical Study of Spatial Memory Staleness in VLM Agents, 2026-08-05, found on the HF channel and missed by the proposal's own check) documents that agents act on stale spatial memory without detecting it, which pre-empts a good part of P3's phenomenon in a different modality, though without item-level intervention value or the location-clause-edit ablation. arXiv:2608.17050 (Cross-Model Memory Transfer via Target-Side Reader Adaptation, verified) shows cross-reader memory reuse is already an active question, but for engram-style parametric memory at aggregate accuracy, not for per-item utilities of a text store.
strongest_objection: The headline asymmetry is built into the class construction, and the proposal's own control does not remove it. The EP class is defined by positive nested-k position value in the reference reader's existing logs and then further cut at |REPLACE-static| >= 10 net in R1; the W class is planted by the authors with no reader-derived selection at all. A quantity selected on reader A's outcomes must regress when reader A is replaced, whereas a constructed class cannot regress, so L_EP >> L_W is close to arithmetic. The proposed same-reader replication L_RR (R1 vs R2) only nets out the seed-family regression of the |value| >= 10 cut - both cells use the same reader, so it is blind to the prior, class-defining selection stage. A reviewer will read P1 as measuring winner's curse across readers rather than a property of help versus harm. Two further predictions cannot be decided at the stated power: P4's whole decision zone (0.20 predicted, 0.10 falsifier) sits inside the stated SE of 0.06 for a difference of Spearmans (95% half-width ~0.12), and P1's third clause (W under B <= -10 vs falsifier >= -5) sits inside the cell's own +/-4.5 CI - the proposal states both problems but does not fix either. P5's cost ordering is likewise favoured by construction: criterion K shares reader, item set and estimator (REPLACE-static) with the intervention route and differs only in composition and seed family, while the re-learning route shares only the retrieval regime, so shared method variance, not cost efficiency, can produce the predicted gap; the episode accounting also compares probing 40 chosen items against learning a Q over the whole store.
what_would_fix_it: (1) Define the EP class by a reader-independent criterion - item content (type-matched expert procedures sampled without regard to measured value), or a third reader's logs - and keep the value-selected version only as a secondary, explicitly winner's-curse-labelled arm. (2) Add the symmetric transfer cell: select items on reader B's measured values and measure the loss back on reader A. If help is genuinely reader-specific the loss is large in both directions; if the effect is selection, the asymmetry reverses with the direction of selection. This is the single cheapest change that turns P1 from near-entailed into a real test, and cell (c) already serves reader B. (3) Restate P4 on the EP-only correlation and size it to at least two SE, or drop it to a reported estimand. (4) For P5, add a second criterion under reader B measured by a different estimator (REMOVE-based, or a realized pruning outcome) and require the cost ordering to hold against both; count route (i)'s episodes for the full item set it would have to re-rank in deployment. (5) Make the unforced grown-store cell (h) the confirmatory arm for P2 and report the forced-self-written-top-1 re-run separately, so 'growth did not change the retrieved set' stays a reportable falsifier.
missing_baseline: The reverse-direction transfer cell - select the helpful class on reader B's own measured values and measure retained value back on reader A - together with a content-matched, non-value-selected expert control class (random same-type expert items) run through R1/R2/B. Without either, the plan cannot distinguish 'help is reader-specific' from 'value-selected items regress under any re-measurement with a new reader', which is the reading a reviewer will default to. Secondary omission: a third reader, so that P1 is not a statement about one Qwen3-32B -> Qwen3-14B (or Llama-3.1-8B) pair; the pre-registered fallback of a thinking-on/off decoding swap is not a consumer swap at all and would leave the headline untested if E0's band gate fails.
preprint_collision: No verified collision. The proposal's own check is above average for this round - six labelled queries, IDs given, one candidate (CHIME 2609.02074) verified with s2cli paper, and Q4 correctly reported as empty rather than as evidence - and I found nothing that makes the central asymmetric-transfer claim. My own queries, all answered by channel (a) s2cli (S2 + HF); WebSearch was unavailable in this session and was not used. Q1 [mechanism, --recent] 'memory item utility transfer across reader models re-measure counterfactual value after model swap': nothing relevant (8 hits, all counterfactual-prompting or bias-transfer work). Q2 [mechanism, --recent] 'learned memory utility validity drift agent memory reader swap store growth re-measurement': RoMeRL 2608.02508, Compliance Trap 2607.10608, Memory Reward Inflation 2608.00017, TRUSTMEM 2606.25161, SeqMem-Eval 2605.15384, ReMe 2512.10696 - all aggregate or set-level, none re-measures an item's value after a reader or store change. Q3 [closest named method] 'ExpSuite executor-agnostic experience reuse with without set feedback': returned 2605.30712 under its real title ExpGraph (S2, cit 2). Q4 [cross-executor, --recent] 'experience memory transfers across executor models utility ranking model-agnostic reuse': ExpGraph 2605.30712, Spatial Memory Agent 2608.12743 (across frozen base models, aggregate only), Memory Transfer Learning 2604.14004 (cross-domain, not cross-reader). Q5 [--recent] 'stale memory item harmful helpful asymmetry sign flip counterfactual leave-one-out': When Memory Lies 2608.04574, MemStrata 2606.26511, Memora 2604.20006 - 2608.04574 partly pre-empts P3's stale-location phenomenon and the proposal's check missed it. Q6 [home] 'transfer of data valuation influence scores across models rank correlation': nothing on cross-model transfer of attribution scores, confirming the proposal's Q4/Q5 finding. Q7 [home] 'active probing to re-estimate item utility cheaper than relearning sample cost curve': empty of anything close to P5. Two weaknesses in the proposal's check: it names 2605.30712 'ExpSuite' when S2 indexes it as ExpGraph - and that is the very paper whose executor-agnostic claim the proposal exists to overturn, so getting its identity wrong is not cosmetic - and it ran no query on the layout-shift/stale-location half or on cross-model memory transfer, the two places where I found live preprints (2608.04574, 2608.17050). IDs I verified this session: 2605.08374 (MemQ), 2606.00547 (MERIT), 2607.22562 (SF-AMS), 2604.20006 (Memora), 2605.18565 (MINTEval), 2604.27003, 2607.10608, 2609.02074 (CHIME), 2608.02508 (RoMeRL), 2608.17050, 2512.10696 (ReMe), 2410.13850 (LDS/influence for diffusion), 2505.18513 (AirRep). Only 2605.30712 failed direct id lookup; it was confirmed instead through two S2 search hits, with a title that differs from the proposal's.
